transcript.text: Just had a new induction hob fitted, Beko. When I put my saucepan on it just flashes a U and doesn't heat. Is it faulty? It's brand new!!

Good news: it's almost certainly not faulty. On Beko induction hobs (and many other brands), a flashing "U" means "no suitable pan detected." The hob is working. It just doesn't recognise your saucepan.

Common causes:

1. The pan isn't induction-compatible (most likely). Induction only works with magnetic cookware. Aluminium, copper, glass, ceramic, and some stainless steel pans won't work.
• Quick test: hold a fridge magnet to the bottom of the pan. If it sticks firmly, it should work. If it doesn't stick or only barely clings, the pan isn't suitable.
• Also look for the induction symbol (a coil-like zigzag) on the base or packaging.

2. The pan is too small for the zone. Each zone needs a minimum base diameter to detect the pan. Try a smaller zone, or a bigger pan.

3. The pan isn't centred. Line it up with the circle marking the zone.

4. The base is warped or not flat. A pan that rocks or has a domed base may not make good enough contact.

5. The pan was placed after the zone was switched on and timed out. Put the pan on first, then select the zone and power level. If you take too long, the zone switches itself off.

What to do: Try the magnet test, and if you have any cast iron or enamelled steel pans (like a Le Creuset-style casserole), try one of those. Those almost always work. If a definitely-magnetic, properly sized, centred pan still gives you a flashing U on every zone, contact Beko or your installer, since the hob is under warranty.

If your pans fail the magnet test, you can either buy induction-ready cookware or get an induction converter disc (a flat magnetic plate that sits between hob and pan). The disc works but is slower and less efficient, so it's best as a stopgap or for a favourite pan you don't want to replace.
I tried the magnet and it doesn't stick to my saucepans! It does stick to my cast-iron casserole though, and that did heat up fine.

That settles it: your hob is working perfectly, and the problem is your saucepans. They're probably aluminium or non-magnetic stainless steel, which induction can't heat.

Your options:

1. Buy induction-compatible pans (best long-term fix)
• Look for the induction coil symbol or "suitable for all hobs, including induction" on the packaging.
• Take a fridge magnet shopping with you. If it sticks firmly to the base, you're good.
• Good materials: cast iron, enamelled steel, magnetic stainless steel, or aluminium pans with a bonded magnetic base (very common and usually lighter and cheaper).
• A basic set of 3 saucepans and a frying pan is usually enough to get going.

2. Use an induction converter disc (stopgap)
• Sits on the hob and lets you use your existing pans.
• Slower, less efficient, and the disc gets very hot, so it's handy temporarily but not great for everyday cooking.

3. Keep using what works
• Your cast-iron casserole is fine for soups, stews, boiling pasta, and more while you sort out new pans.

Quick tips for your new hob:
• Induction is much faster than gas or ceramic, so start on lower settings than you're used to, especially for frying.
• Lift pans rather than sliding them to avoid scratching the glass.
• Cast iron works brilliantly but is heavy, so place it down gently.

Enjoy the new hob. Once you've got the right pans, you'll probably love how quick it is!
